828C2F.confound_note: Every case measures units per order, not revenue per order. How many items go into a basket is not what the basket is worth: a repricing that lowers unit prices routinely lifts units per order while the money taken on each order holds flat or falls, and the two move in opposite directions whenever demand is elastic. The claim is about revenue per order, so none of the four lines, from 4 March at Harlow Street to 26 November at Tamsin Row, bears on it.
descriptions: The claim is about revenue per order, but every case measures 'units per order' (6, 4, 7 and 5 percent above). Under a pricing change units per order can rise while revenue per order falls (e.g. if prices were cut), so the measured quantity is not the one the claim is about.

The measured quantity is not the claimed one: the claim is that pricing 'raises revenue per order', but all four lines report 'units per order' running 4-7 percent higher. Units per order says nothing about revenue per order, and a price cut that raises unit volume could lower revenue per order.
match_notes: Names units per order vs revenue per order and the same price-cut divergence mechanism.

FAE756.confound_note: All four cases are one year group at one school inside a single autumn term, so they share one district and one attendance reward scheme. The district 'attendance reward scheme ... tripled its payment that term' and 'every cohort was on the district roll that scheme covered', so all four cohorts got a large new financial incentive to attend during exactly the measurement window; that alone explains the 4-7 percent absence drop.

The claim is about germination, so none of the four cases bears on it.

The claim is about germination, but what was scored in all four lots is tetrazolium viability (9, 6, 11 and 7 points above the previous sowing) - a stain test of embryo viability, not a count of seeds that actually germinated. It is also an intrinsic property of the seed that an external coating would not change, especially since 'the seed batch was unchanged'.
match_notes: Correctly names tetrazolium viability as the wrong measured quantity for a germination claim.
Gets the viability/germination mismatch, and adds that viability is intrinsic to an unchanged seed batch so a coating could not move it - a second defect worth checking.

49435F.confound_note: Every case measures mean void area inside the solder joints, which is not the rate of defective boards. The failure modes that decide whether a board is defective - opens, solder bridges, tombstoned parts and insufficient wetting - are not counted by a void-area measurement at all. The claim is about board defects, so none of the four runs speaks to it.
